---
title: "Engineering School HPC Cluster"
description: "The UC School of Engineering cluster: getting an account, logging in, SSH keys, moving files, and usage rules."
---

The UC School of Engineering (Escuela de Ingeniería) runs a high-performance
computing (HPC) cluster for teaching and research. Lab members can get an
account through Tomás. Use it for jobs that are too big or too long for your
laptop.

- **Official page:** [dt.ing.uc.cl/recursos/cluster](https://dt.ing.uc.cl/recursos/cluster/)
  (in Spanish, maintained by the School's Dirección de Tecnología, DT)
- **Login address:** `cluster.ing.uc.cl`
- **Job scheduler:** SLURM, see [Running Jobs on the Cluster](cluster-jobs.qmd)
- **Help desk:** [7500@uc.cl](mailto:7500@uc.cl), for platform problems only

This page summarizes the DT page as of November 2026. If something here
doesn't match the DT page, trust the DT page and update this one.

## What's available {#partitions}

Compute nodes are grouped into partitions. You choose one when you submit a
job.

| Partition | Hardware | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| `full` | 1 Intel node: 32 cores, 128 GB RAM | Same for all users |
| `512x1024` | 5 AMD EPYC nodes: 64–128 cores and 256–512 GB RAM each | Open to all; groups that paid for the nodes go first |
| `gpus` | 2 Intel nodes with 11 NVIDIA GPUs in total (9 Quadro RTX 8000 and 1 RTX 6000 Ada, 48 GB each; 1 Quadro RTX 6000, 24 GB), 1.5–2 TB RAM per node | Open to all; groups that paid for the nodes go first |

The DT page writes the AMD partition as both `512X1024` and `512x1024`. Its
example scripts use `512x1024`. SLURM names are case-sensitive, so run
`sinfo` on the cluster to see the exact current names and which nodes are
free.

## Getting an account {#getting-an-account}

A full-time School of Engineering professor has to request each account, and
for lab members that's Tomás. Send him:

- Your full name and institutional email
- The software you need to run (for example R, Python, MATLAB)
- How long you need the account (the date it can be deleted)
- Your level: undergraduate, master's, PhD, postdoc, research assistant
- The purpose, for example "IPRE", "Master's thesis", or a Fondecyt project
  number
- Your department, institute, or center

Tomás emails the request to the help desk, and the help desk sends you your
username and password.

DT lists each account's purpose on its public website. Keep it short and
generic ("Master's thesis"). Don't describe unpublished results.

## Logging in {#logging-in}

Open a terminal: Terminal on macOS and Linux, or
[Windows Terminal](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9n0dx20hk701) on Windows
(built into Windows 11). Then run:

```bash
ssh username@cluster.ing.uc.cl
```

Replace `username` with the username the help desk sent you. The first time,
SSH asks you to confirm the server's identity: type `yes`. Nothing appears
on screen while you type your password, which is normal. Type `exit` to log
out.

You land on the **login node**, a shared machine for editing files, submitting
jobs, and quick tests. DT cancels heavy programs running there. Run analyses
as jobs, and install software from an
[interactive session](cluster-jobs.qmd#interactive) on a compute node.

You don't need the UC VPN to log in over SSH from off campus. The
[monitoring dashboards](#monitoring) are different: they only open from the
UC network (wired or eduroam).

## Logging in without a password {#ssh-keys}

An SSH key saves you from typing your password every time. If you already
made a key, for example for [GitHub](../tutorials/git-github.qmd), reuse it
and skip `ssh-keygen`.

**macOS and Linux:**

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519        # press Enter to accept the default location
ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub username@cluster.ing.uc.cl
ssh username@cluster.ing.uc.cl   # should no longer ask for your password
```

**Windows** has no `ssh-copy-id`, so you copy the key and add it by hand. Run
these from your home folder, where Windows Terminal opens:

```powershell
ssh-keygen -t ed25519
scp .ssh/id_ed25519.pub username@cluster.ing.uc.cl:
ssh username@cluster.ing.uc.cl "mkdir -p .ssh; cat id_ed25519.pub >> .ssh/authorized_keys; rm id_ed25519.pub"
ssh username@cluster.ing.uc.cl
```

`ssh-keygen` also asks for a passphrase. DT suggests leaving it empty. A
passphrase protects the key if someone gets your laptop, and your system's
keychain or `ssh-agent` can remember it for you.

Your private key (`id_ed25519`, without `.pub`) never leaves your computer.
Don't share it, email it, or commit it.

### A shortcut name {#ssh-config}

Add this to `~/.ssh/config` on your computer (on Windows,
`C:\Users\<you>\.ssh\config`; create the file if it doesn't exist):

```
Host uc-cluster
    HostName cluster.ing.uc.cl
    User username
```

After that, `ssh uc-cluster` logs you in, and `uc-cluster:` works in place of
`username@cluster.ing.uc.cl:` in `scp` commands.

## Moving files {#moving-files}

Use `scp` from a terminal on **your computer**, not on the cluster. The colon
marks the cluster side; nothing after it means your home folder.

```bash
# Upload a file or folder to your home folder on the cluster
scp -r my-folder username@cluster.ing.uc.cl:

# Upload into a folder in your cluster account
scp -r my-folder username@cluster.ing.uc.cl:projects/

# Download from the cluster into the current folder
scp -r username@cluster.ing.uc.cl:projects/results .
```

If you prefer a graphical tool, [FileZilla](https://filezilla-project.org/)
works: connect with SFTP to `cluster.ing.uc.cl`, port 22, with your cluster
username. The DT page links short videos (in Spanish) for `scp` and FileZilla.

## Storage {#storage}

- Everything lives in your home folder. The DT page doesn't describe a
  separate scratch space.
- There's no hard quota, but DT asks you to stay under **100 GB**. A daily
  check emails you when you go over.
- Delete temporary files, and move results off the cluster when a job
  finishes.
- **Don't count on the cluster for backups.** Its backup disks only protect
  against hardware failure, and DT isn't responsible for lost data. Keep code
  in GitHub and a copy of important results somewhere else.

## Rules {#rules}

DT's usage policy, in short:

- Use the cluster for teaching and research.
- Share fairly. There are few hard limits, but DT stops jobs that take over
  the cluster.
- Run only licensed software. Unlicensed software is prohibited.
- You're responsible for making sure your data are legal to use there. DT
  names medical records, contact details, and personal ID numbers (RUT) as
  examples.
- DT staff can access every file on the cluster to give support or detect
  illegal activity. Using the cluster means you accept this.

**Ask Tomás before you copy controlled-access data (such as
[ADNI](../databases/adni.qmd) or [ROSMAP](../databases/rosmap.qmd)) or
participant data to the cluster.** It's a shared university system that
other people administer. The data use agreement or ethics approval has to
allow storing the data there. See
[AI Tools and Lab Data](../data/ai-tools-and-lab-data.qmd) for the same
reasoning applied to AI tools.

## Monitoring dashboards {#monitoring}

Both open only from the UC network.

- [Ganglia](https://ganglia.ing.puc.cl/ganglia/): live CPU and memory use per
  node
- [Open XDMoD](https://xdmod.ing.puc.cl:8080/): usage per user and per
  account, built from SLURM records (GPU use isn't included)

## Getting help {#help}

- **Can't log in, a node is down, or something is wrong with the cluster
  itself:** email the help desk at [7500@uc.cl](mailto:7500@uc.cl) or use
  [mesadeayuda.ing.uc.cl](https://mesadeayuda.ing.uc.cl).
- **Your code fails or your job doesn't do what you expected:** the help desk
  doesn't support user programs. Ask in the lab or ask Tomás.
